description_full: PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk operates as a food solutions company in Indonesia, rest of Asia, Africa, and internationally. The company operates through Consumer Branded Products Business Group, Bogasari Business Group, Agribusiness Group, and Distribution Business Group segments. It provides consumer branded products, such as noodles, dairy products, snack food, food seasonings, nutrition and special food, and beverages. The company also offers flexible and corrugated packaging products; and produces and sells wheat flour and pasta. In addition, it engages in the seed breeding and oil palm cultivation and milling; manufacturing and marketing of cooking oils, margarine, and shortening products; and cultivation of sugar cane, rubber, and other crops, as well as distributes consumer products manufactured by third parties. The company was formerly known as PT Panganjaya Intikusuma and changed its name to PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk in January 1994. The company was incorporated in 1990 and is headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia. PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk operates as a subsidiary of First Pacific Investment Management Limited.

financial_summary: PT INDOFOOD SUKSES MAKMUR TBK is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.5B market cap on $6.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 6% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 33%.
The business throws off $768M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.8×.

Shareholder yield of 3.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 59% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
